meta.voice: Editorial feature with a critic's eye. Third person, original wording.
meta.note: Plot beats follow the supplied notes. Critique lines are readings of structure and theme drawn from those beats, not review scores.

chapters.title: This is Tomorrow
chapters.headline: The Storm Arrives on a Floppy Disk
chapters.summary: London, March 1966, and two rival organizations are sprinting toward the same prize. Agents of Manus Vindictae and of the St. Pavlov Foundation both want a pirate-radio DJ who calls herself Captain Regulus, and she is doing her best to vanish, with a talking, floating apple named APPLe for company. Vertin, the Foundation's Timekeeper, and her assistant Sonetto cheat the odds with a floppy disk labelled TeLEPorT, which pinpoints Regulus and lets them talk her toward Vertin's suitcase. A rooftop-to-alley chase across the city follows, ending with Vertin bundling the DJ and the apple inside seconds before the Storm sweeps through and reverses time on everything outside.
chapters.critique: The opener plays like a caper, and that is the smart choice: by the time the Storm lands, the audience has already learned that the suitcase means safety. Lightness first, dread second.

chapters.title: In Our Time
chapters.headline: A Hotel Full of Masks
chapters.summary: The suitcase opens onto Chicago, 1929. Sonetto carries a mission with a deadline: stop the massacre of Arcanists planned for less than a week away. A woman named Schneider is already ahead of her, gunning down local gangsters who persecute Arcanists before they can act. Regulus and APPLe turn up evidence of a meeting at the Walden Hotel downtown. Vertin approaches it on foot through a forest, where a strange woman named Druvis III lives, while Sonetto hitches a ride with Sotheby, a wealthy, potion-brewing Arcanist whose startled driver ploughs into the hotel's back wall and exposes a hidden passage. Inside, Manus Vindictae's leaders, Arcana and Forget Me Not, are speeding up the Great Depression to hasten the Storm, and they use the panic of the rich guests to sell them masks that promise protection but turn the wearers into mindless servants. Sotheby and the Foundation's Arcanists try to herd the innocent out, and run into Druvis III, who is working for the other side.
chapters.critique: Villainy here is financial before it is magical. The mask is the chapter's central image: protection offered at the cost of the self, a bargain the story keeps returning to.

chapters.title: Tender is the Night
chapters.headline: The Last Supper Is Made of Gold
chapters.summary: Sotheby gets most of the group out of the Walden, but Vertin and Schneider are left behind. Arcana wants Vertin to join her, and to make the case she locks her inside a dream in which Vertin plays happily with Schneider, never realizing that in the waking world she is firing Schneider's own gun into the real woman again and again. Across town, Sotheby returns to a mansion that has gone strangely quiet. Her butler, Mr. Karson, serves dinner, and the meal is gold, jewels and dollar bills, while reports spread of a similar sickness across the Chicago area as the Storm closes in. Back at the hotel, Vertin talks Druvis III into helping her escape, and Schneider has somehow survived because her heart sits on the opposite side of her chest. They reach a charred forest, which Sonetto's group is also heading toward after Madam Z at the Foundation tells them supplies are being routed to a refugee camp there. Both parties converge as Forget Me Not and Arcana announce the Storm's arrival. Manus Vindictae reaches its goal before anyone can stop it. The survivors retreat to the mansion for one last supper from Mr. Karson, and then the Storm takes every non-Arcanist, Schneider included.
chapters.critique: The dream sequence is the chapter's cruellest device, turning the reader's comfort into the instrument of harm. The golden dinner is the lighter, stranger counterpart: absurd on the plate, devastating as a metaphor for what greed has left to eat.

chapters.title: Nouvelles et Textes pour Rien
chapters.headline: A School Song Goes Off-Script
chapters.location: School for the Primary Defense of Mankind
chapters.summary: A gifted girl named Vertin, a star pupil at the School for the Primary Defense of Mankind, is shut in an isolation room after asking her principal, in public, about the Storm. Together with a band of fellow troublemakers she decides to rebel against the school's strict teachers and administrators. The first move is a school song that wanders off its lyrics while keeping the same tune, and the students do not realize they are singing Manus Vindictae propaganda, which brings the principal down on them with a heavy hand. The second move is the escape itself, a plan to slip past the guards and teachers and reach the outside world. What Vertin does not know is that she is playing into the hands of Constantine, the Foundation's Director, who lets her and her friends through the walls just as the Storm hits. Every friend who reaches the exit disappears with the rain, and Vertin is the only one left. Madam Z then appears at the gate and offers her the chance to become the Timekeeper officially.
chapters.critique: This is the story's origin wound, and it is built on irony: a child's rebellion turns out to be someone else's plan. Notably, the horror comes less from the Storm than from an adult who judges the children's deaths an acceptable price.

chapters.title: El Oro de los Tigres
chapters.headline: The Shadow War Over One Girl
chapters.summary: Vertin is reliving her past under 'Artificial Somnambulism', a procedure supervised by her former classmate Mesmer Jr. Meanwhile Constantine and Madam Z debate what to do with Sonetto and the other Arcanists who arrived inside the suitcase. Druvis III, Sotheby and Regulus decide to push back against the Foundation, which they see as holding them without their consent, or Vertin's. While they resist openly, Madam Z and Sonetto quietly open a shadow war against Constantine, aiming to free Vertin and give the Timekeeper more independence, with a peaceful settlement as the hope. Lilya, for her part, finds herself drawn to Vertin's side.
chapters.critique: A chapter about consent, told through bureaucracy and covert maneuvering rather than set-piece combat. The war here is over who gets to decide things for the Timekeeper.

chapters.title: The Prisoner in the Cave
chapters.headline: Arithmetic Island
chapters.location: An island in the Aegean Sea
chapters.summary: With Vertin rescued and an amendment passed to give her more autonomy from Constantine and the Foundation, Madam Z sends the group, plus Regulus and Lilya, to an old Manus Vindictae base where Olitiaus were once kept, a site the Storm somehow left unreversed. They find a sentient radio, decode its messages and learn their next stop: the Gorgon Current in the Aegean. Regulus is delighted to be given a new boat, APPLe II, but it is attacked and the survivors scatter. Vertin washes up on a beach where a blue-haired woman tells her she has fixed her watch, and that the year is 2007. The group regathers on a strange island of Pythagoreans, who treat mathematical logic as the highest form of existence, to the point that nearly all of them are named with numbers. Arcana has landed there too, with a handful of followers, and Sonetto lashes out at her and gets into trouble. Vertin turns the island's own logic to save her, Lilya breaks Regulus out of the cell she was locked in for breaking a taboo, and both sides try to work out why Arcana came and what she wants.
chapters.critique: Rule-bound societies make good traps for protagonists, and this one lets the heroes win by playing the island's logic against itself. The wrong year on a stranger's wristwatch is the quietest and best unsettling detail.

chapters.title: E lucevan le stelle
chapters.headline: Opera for an Empire's Last Summer
chapters.summary: In 1914 the island is exposed to the outside world, and several nations start fighting over it with warplanes. Elsewhere, the Foundation sends two History Guards, Hofmann and Marcus, to Vienna, part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, where Manus Vindictae leaders have been sighted; the goal is intel on how the Manus survive the Storm before the next catastrophe. The two women contend with the era's prejudice and superstition, and with Mr. Karl, the unpleasant head of the Foundation's Vienna branch. Their leads are a museum curator named Heinrich, an unlicensed therapist named Kakania, and a traumatized opera singer, Isolde, who can summon possessive spirits and may be the centre of it all. After Marcus rescues Kakania from a rigged duel, Kakania begins treating Isolde and urges her to stop suppressing her trauma and desires. Isolde takes the advice to heart, and Heinrich manipulates her into using her powers to rouse Arcanists and the downtrodden of Austria-Hungary to revolt, which speeds the Storm toward them. Vienna becomes a bloodbath, Hofmann is killed and Kakania blames herself. Marcus persuades her to look into Isolde's mind for the last lead; Kakania draws out the ritual Arcana used to shield her chosen few from the Storm, Marcus reads it with her own arcana, and the three women run for safety.
chapters.critique: An opera in structure as well as setting: an overpowered voice, a manipulated heroine, a collapse that nobody intended. The tragedy is built from good advice carried too far, which makes it harder to dismiss.

chapters.title: Vereinsamt
chapters.headline: A Knot Against the Storm
chapters.location: The Foundation and the Aegean island
chapters.summary: At the Foundation, Lucy and the staff of the Laplace Scientific Computing Center work to decode Marcus's transmission in search of a Storm antidote. Their first attempts at the ritual kill several Foundation staff, and Enigma, furious, clashes with Lucy over the research. On the island, 37 wakes from a coma a week after its exposure, to find it can no longer fully shelter its people from the Storm. She and Vertin go back into the cave to face the trials of Apeiron, hoping to find a way past the Storm, but Vienna has hurried the First World War along, and the great powers resume fighting over the island. As bombs fall, Apeiron's followers break in body and mind, and some defect to Arcana. Sophia snaps at 37 and discovers her own number is an irrational one, then leaves with the new Manus recruits. Arcana remains, saying she stayed for Vertin. Vertin, who has spent too long planning Arcana's elimination to turn back, goes through with it: Regulus, Lilya and Sonetto flush Arcana out, Zeno teleports her to a deserted site, and a thermobaric bomb is dropped on her. Admiral Igor of Zeno thinks he hears a faint sound, writes it off as wind from the blast, and declares Arcana dead. With the Storm due again within hours, the Foundation's leaders, 37 and the surviving followers attempt a ritual to let everyone live through it unharmed. When Vertin reads the original ritual as 'The First Circle', 37 is inspired and produces a knot design that satisfies its conditions. Lucy tests it and lets the design slip to Kakania, who spreads it as widely as she can. The Storm hits and most people holding the knot survive, but 37 watches in shock as followers celebrating a Bacchanalia on the beach, beyond the island's protection, vanish, along with most of the wreckage from the battle. Vertin returns to the Foundation with 37, Regulus and Sonetto. Lilya and Druvis III receive medals, Mesmer Jr. gives Vertin a new umbrella made with the knot ritual, Marcus is given a copy and asks to return to the field, and Lucy is pushed out of Laplace for her accumulated actions over Enigma's objections, with the rest of the organization saluting her on the way out.
chapters.critique: The longest and most ambitious chapter in the opening arc, and it deliberately refuses a clean win. Arcana's apparent death is undercut by a single dismissed sound, and the survival of the knot is shadowed by the Bacchanalia on the beach. The closing salute to Lucy is a small, dignified beat in a chapter that mostly lives on large ones.
contentNotes: Deaths of named and unnamed characters

chapters.title: Tristes Tropiques
chapters.headline: Mutiny on the River Tietê
chapters.summary: The Timekeeper travels to Brazil to follow a lead on 'Urd', bringing Sotheby and Lilya. They meet Admiral Igor and his adopted daughter Lopera as they execute several Zeno traitors, and learn that the Order of Enlightenment and the Apostles Brotherhood, both offshoots of Manus Vindictae, have been infiltrating Zeno units and talking them into mutiny. Lilya is left at the base while Vertin, Sotheby and Lopera head by boat down the Tietê toward São Paulo and a Zeno veterans' residence where a blind doctor reportedly treats the locals, but curiosity takes them first to a locked tower, where Vertin accidentally breaks a seal. On the boat she meets Ms. Kimberly, whom she had encountered at Tuesday's Motel, who turns out to want nothing more than some stolen bread, while Lopera plays a game with a preacher named Santos. Pirates then attack and sink the boat. Sotheby washes ashore inside a large fish caught by Mr. Duncan, who strikingly resembles her late butler Karson, though he denies any connection, and he takes her to a favela where the Apostles Brotherhood is recruiting. After Sotheby publicly denounces Santos, Duncan creates a scene to work his way into the group. Vertin, saved from drowning by Kimberly but made ill by polluted water, is rescued by Doctor Dores while she treats children in a favela. Mercado, a mercenary employed by Santos, captures Dores in exchange for everyone else's lives. Lopera and Duncan infiltrate the Brotherhood, free one of Duncan's friends, and join Vertin's group at the veterans' residence to plan Dores's rescue. The next day Admiral Igor launches his own plan with loyal lieutenants Moldir and Ptolemy: tired of fighting what he sees as a losing battle, he intends to defect to Manus Vindictae. He tells Lilya he believes Arcana is alive, then has her jailed on a pretext, though Moldir leaves orders to free her when the shooting starts and Arcanist Zeno soldiers open fire on their human comrades. In São Paulo, Ptolemy uses a wind-up toy from San Francisco as a totem to force Kimberly to kill Vertin; Kimberly resists, but is compelled to throttle her, until Vertin grabs a pistol and shoots through the toy, breaking the hold and freeing Kimberly to take revenge on nearby Zeno soldiers. Elsewhere, Lopera defeats Santos and rescues Dores, but Moldir's troops arrive to take Dores into custody and Moldir tries to recruit Lopera. When Lopera refuses to join Igor's plot, Moldir shoots her with a round that turns out to be a tranquilizer. The group regroups and tries to recover Dores, but too many traitorous Zeno soldiers block the way, and Igor takes Moldir and the doctor to Tierra del Fuego. There he meets the Preacher, who is revealed to be Sophia and who insists on her own terms; Igor agrees and takes a certain container in exchange. Back at Foundation headquarters, Duncan is questioned about his resemblance to Karson, Lilya hints that Moldir might be persuaded to come back, Constantine discusses recent developments with the President of the Pax Security Council, and a heartbroken Lopera empties her gun into a wall.
chapters.critique: The story moves from fantasy to politics here, and the Manus read less like cultists than like organizers who exploit grievance and exhaustion. Igor's betrayal works because it is framed as fatigue rather than evil. The final image of Lopera firing at a wall until the gun is empty says more than any speech could.

chapters.title: Folie et Déraison
chapters.headline: A Prison That Writes Itself
chapters.summary: After Igor's betrayal in Brazil, and after the events aboard the Free Breeze, Vertin and Sonetto go to Ushuaia to pick up Dores's trail before Manus Vindictae can complete its plans for her. A struggling writer named Recoleta tells them Dores set off toward Comala Prison, notorious home of criminally insane Arcanists. Recoleta wants in herself, so she guides the pair there, and Vertin persuades the jailer, a talking jaguar, to open the door. Comala is not an ordinary prison. A panopticon looms at its centre, but the prisoners have formed their own literary society, La Sociedad de Poetas de las Américas, led by a man called The Idealist. Vertin hopes to find Dores, Recoleta hopes to find her pen pal Aleph, and both must dig into the Society and the truths buried in Comala. Eventually the three women gain an audience with The Physician, who runs the prison as warden. He reveals that he and The Idealist are two aspects of Aleph, the true warden of Comala, a human who was given a special die holding vast Arcane power by Manus Vindictae. Once Recoleta accepts her own identity as a storyteller, Aleph points Vertin and Sonetto to a nearby boat that carried Dores and other Manus figures to a hidden base at the South Pole, and they set off at once. Behind them, the Panopticon collapses with nobody left to watch it, the formerly compliant prisoners spill into Ushuaia, and the jailer, with her purpose gone, lies down in the flames of the burning prison.
chapters.critique: Comala is a prison of books, and the chapter is at its best when it treats storytelling as both confinement and escape. The warden who splits himself into rival personas is a neat answer to the panopticon, and the jailer's quiet end after the watching stops is its sharpest image.

chapters.title: Paradise Regained
chapters.headline: The Flood at the End of the World
chapters.summary: The Foundation and its Zeno forces race to the South Pole to stop Manus Vindictae from finishing its master plan, but the Manus have magical beasts and Zeno defectors led by Admiral Igor and Moldir guarding the coast. On one stretch of shoreline, Ulrich and an Arcanist guard try to slip in to support Vertin and are quickly caught by Moldir, who quietly lets them go and even hands them a talking squirrel named Buddy Fairchild as backup. Vertin and Sonetto keep following Dr. Dores's trail across the ice and find the lone survivor of a research station, a woman named Nautika, who has been sending a desperate warning over a broken radio telling everyone to stay away; her mind has been shattered by what she saw and by watching her colleagues die one by one. After an initial fight, Vertin offers to let Nautika hold on to Ms. Radio while the others continue, but Nautika decides to guide them through the snow instead. After a harrowing trek through snow, caves, dire wolves and a maze, and with help from a highly placed mole, Ms. Stranger, they locate the Manus ritual site. At the gate Nautika watches one of her friends be sacrificed to open the chamber. The group has to fight its way in but cannot get through before the gate closes, and Nautika sacrifices herself so the others can pass. Inside, Sonetto fights Sophia while Vertin finds Dr. Dores beside an arcane spinning wheel like the one in her suitcase. The ritual has already begun. Arcana, supposedly dead, appears in a new body and unleashes a Storm stronger than anything the Foundation prepared for, called the Flood, which she says will return the world to a primeval age ruled by Arcanists. As humans are washed away across the Arctic, Vertin nearly dies, but Dores helps her smash the spinning wheel before the Flood can finish her.
chapters.critique: A finale that raises the stakes from a city to the planet while keeping its best scenes small: Moldir's quiet mercy, Nautika's choice at the gate. Arcana's return in a new body is the less surprising beat, since the previous arc planted the doubt, but it pays off the unease left by the faint sound in Chapter 7.

chapters.title: A Long Long Way
chapters.headline: Peace Table, War Table
chapters.summary: Vertin stopped the Manus ritual from flooding the Earth, but Arcana is back. The Foundation and Vertin's allies now find themselves in an alternate 1920 in which the First World War is still going. While trying to end it quickly, the Foundation is split between the Doves, who want both sides at the negotiating table before things get worse, and the Hawks, who say no progress is possible until Manus Vindictae is wiped out. Initial talks collapse when a French sniper assassinates a German colonel. In a German trench, a wounded soldier nicknamed Charon walks the lines collecting mementos from the fallen on every side, trying to keep his last living friend from sliding into bloodlust now that the friend commands the troops. Nearby, a Foundation agent and field medic named Marsha meets the French sniper, who admits she shot the colonel after finding evidence that the Manus were influencing him to prolong the war. Later, Sentinel helps Marsha, rescuing her from an armoured car and from soldiers also swayed by the Manus. Cold at first, Sentinel warms to Marsha and invites her to meet her family of gargoyles, who have each been affected by the war in different ways. Soon after, Sentinel gives Marsha a stack of documents exposing Manus collaborators on both sides. Marsha hands them to the Foundation, which uses them to bring the world's leaders back to the table at Montpaix. The troops on the front cheer, thinking peace has arrived, but the Manus show their hand with an attack on Montpaix that kills soldiers, negotiators and Foundation personnel. The Foundation's XII detachment, a special forces team led by Creius, repels the first wave, and the second is a battalion of Arcanist Manus soldiers striking both German and French lines. Creius rallies survivors from both armies against them and gives Sentinel explosives to destroy the Manus's underground base. Sentinel faces her own private hell inside it, accepting that she may become a demon if that is what it takes to save more lives, and succeeds in blowing up the base. Creius leads the troops to victory, Marsha heals everyone she can, and Charon keeps walking the battlefield.
chapters.critique: A war chapter that treats ceasefire as the thing in danger, not the thing already achieved. The cross-lines cooperation against the Manus is the emotional payoff, and Charon's wandering, collecting small remnants of the dead, is the chapter's recurring image of grief with no one to give it to.

chapters.title: The Campaign's Tale
chapters.headline: Warm Weather on the Don
chapters.summary: Russia in the 1920s. The fields along the Don River are going barren under unnaturally warm weather, and bandits are multiplying across the steppe. Zeno Commander Ivan leads a force of Cossacks against both that threat and the Manus Vindictae forces trying to profit from the chaos. Things get worse when the bandits acquire weapons that should not exist in this era and are led by a traitorous Zeno officer named Krutov. The split also opens an opportunity: the turncoat Admiral Igor offers to join forces with Ivan to crush both threats. Meanwhile the Timekeeper travels there to see Igor and follow one of her few remaining leads on Urd, and learns more than she intended. Lilya leads a new flight of strike witches to destroy the latest Manus ritual, but still wants revenge on Igor for what he did in São Paulo.
chapters.critique: The most compact chapter in the main line, and a deliberate pivot: it ties Igor's betrayal and Lilya's grudge to the Urd lead, so that three open threads converge on one steppe.

events.title: The Theft of the Rimet Cup
events.headline: A Heist With Good Manners and Bad Security
events.summary: March 1966, London. The Rimet Cup, football's highest honour, is on show in a museum guarded by Iverson, head of New Humans Security, and his fleet of semi-autonomous robots, which he swears are programmed against every method a thief could try. The display draws four Arcanists with four agendas. Diggers, a hippie with bubble-based psychedelics, sees a stage for his art and his ideals of peace and freedom. Melania Ramirez, a student who moonlights as the Great Thief Acey, wants the cup as revenge on Iverson, who humiliated her father and ruined his security firm. Pickles, a hyper-intelligent dog dragged along by Mr. Charlton and the other pets, would rather read philosophy. And Regulus, convinced the robots are part of a Manus plot, sets out to sabotage them. Iverson fights to hold the exhibit, even unlocking lethal ammunition for his robots, but Melania pulls off the theft, and leaves the cup where Pickles will later be credited with saving it for the World Cup.
events.critique: Joyful and well-balanced, with a rotating cast of motives that never get in each other's way. The final gag, a dog taking credit for a theft, is the right size of joke.

events.title: A Nightmare at Green Lake
events.headline: Slasher Rules, Arcanist Edition
events.summary: Horropedia, a young Foundation field agent, convinces Vertin, Sonetto and Tooth Fairy to visit the Green Lake campsite, once a summer camp and training ground for Zeno Armaments recruits until everyone mysteriously vanished in the early 1970s. A group of college students is there shooting their own slasher movie. As night falls and a thunderstorm settles in, a strange butcher starts killing the students one by one, following the scripts of famous horror films. The Arcanists have to cooperate to stop the killer and solve the mystery of Green Lake before nobody is left to tell it.
events.critique: A genre exercise that works because it knows the rules it is breaking: the killer follows film scripts, so the investigators can read the genre as a map.

events.title: Journey to Mor Pankh
events.headline: A Festival, a Mentor and a Ticking Clock
events.summary: With the Dipa Festival close, astrologer Kaalaa Baunaa has to find her old mentor, Kumar, before she brings destruction down on the village and everyone in it in the name of Manus Vindictae. Helping her evacuate the town are her old friend Shamane, a snake-charming thief named Kanjira, and the Foundation's Matilda, who arrived for unrelated reasons.
events.critique: A mentor-turned-threat story with a festival as the countdown, and a tidy ensemble that gives each ally a job.

events.title: Revival! The Uluru Games
events.headline: A Girl Made of Heat
events.summary: In 1990s Australia, a young boxer named Spathodea begins to change fast, literally bursting with heat as the spirit of the Ulu flame wakes inside her. Vertin and Ezra try to help while Spathodea travels to Uluru Rock to restart the Uluru Games, a mini-Olympics where Arcanists could compete openly until World War II ended them. Her friend Desert Flannel tries to support her, but a scorned paparazzo's actions draw Bunyips, creatures that feed on lies, and threaten to sabotage the Games before they begin.
events.critique: The metaphor is plain and effective: a body that cannot contain a gift, and a media cycle that feeds a monster. Sports stories live on their stakes, and here the stakes are public truth.

events.title: Notes on Shuori
events.headline: A City That Appears on Demand
events.location: The Russian steppes and Pei City
events.summary: Russian Arcanist Yenisei and blind researcher Bessmert trek across the steppes in search of a powerful arcana called 'Ask and Acquire'. Thrown off course by weather and strange sights, the rest of their team wants to turn back and starts a mutiny. Before they can hurt the two women, the team transforms into wild horses and is led off by a man with the body of a bird. Yenisei and Bessmert find Pei City, an ancient Chinese city that appears from nowhere, hoping to find the bird-man and rescue their transformed colleagues.
events.critique: Travelogue meets folktale: the premise is a quest, and the transformation of the mutineers into horses is a neat, wry consequence for those who wanted to quit.

events.title: Farewell, Rayashki
events.headline: A Colony Offered Two Bad Choices
events.summary: In the Arctic Circle near Russia sits an isolated colony called Rayashki, supported for decades by the Zeno Arms Academy in return for mining Runium, a metal vital to magical military vehicles. Now the mines are running dry, critters are spreading and endangering both the operation and the residents, and Zeno, watching costs climb and margins fall, is losing interest. A Zeno delegation arrives and, instead of investing in new infrastructure and exploration, offers two options: leave home and work for Zeno, with the old, sick and young left to Zeno's social services, or turn Rayashki into a military outpost and give up autonomy. Vila, a half-human, half-Rusalka Arcanist, searches for a way to stop Zeno and keep Rayashki independent. One of her students, Avgust, meets researcher Windsong, who tells them about a possible 'limitless source of energy' in Rayashki. With the Zeno delegation pressing for surrender and Chief Security Officer Evgeni's well-meaning but cynical opposition, the residents pull together to try to avoid saying goodbye to their home.
events.critique: A story about corporate attrition rather than a villain, and all the better for it: nobody here is cruel, only indifferent, which makes the colony's stand harder to dismiss.

events.title: Floor It! To the Golden City
events.headline: A Brother, a Key and a Dead Sister
events.summary: In 1990s San Francisco, Joe, known as J, visits his long-lost sister Paulina at the Foundation, and is told she is dead; his last memory of her is a bitter argument over joining the Foundation. Before he can absorb it, he is pulled into a conspiracy involving surviving Manus Vindictae members who have set up in the New Age Market. With help from a young thief who stole their key, and the Foundation's Matilda, who arrived on other business, J and his crew get a chance to stop Apostle Matheus and his followers before their ritual is complete.
events.critique: Grief as an engine: the plot is a heist-shaped excuse for a man to process a quarrel that can no longer be resolved.

events.title: Route 77: The Haunted Highway
events.headline: A Motel With a Pulse
events.summary: In 1990s Texas, bounty hunter Argus and the Timekeeper arrive separately at Tuesday's Motel, each hunting different people and each given a room by Tuesday after being stranded near Route 77. The guests are an odd lot: Tuesday herself, the owner and maid; Ms. Kimberly, refined and hungry; and Stefan, who holds a grudge against Vertin over Arcana's death. While Lilya tries to retrieve her repaired broom from a nearby Zeno base, Argus and Vertin uncover the motel's secrets. Stefan is found dead, having shot himself with a Zeno-made pistol, Ms. Kimberly proves to be the same Manus Vindictae agent Matilda met near San Francisco, and the motel itself turns out to have a beating heart.
events.critique: A locked-building mystery with a supernatural reveal that turns the setting into a character; the motel's heartbeat is the right kind of final twist.

events.title: Chronicles of Uluru: London Dawning
events.headline: Black Fog Over the East End
events.summary: Tooth Fairy is sent to 1930s London to meet Mr. Fog, as the city's fog has turned black and begun infecting humans and Arcanists alike with tuberculosis. Meanwhile the Arcanists of Cross Street in the East End prepare for their Uluru Qualifiers, with vendors and entertainers hoping to profit. As the Londoners try to ignore the black fog and carry on, some Arcanists blame a 'Fog Hag', treating it as a curse rather than a bacterium. As the sickness persists and threatens to cancel the qualifiers, Tooth Fairy and her allies try to meet the so-called Hag, a former Floor Ritualist with a prosthetic leg, and track down the true source of the fog.
events.critique: Superstition against science as a community drama, with a scapegoat figure whose reality is likely to be more sympathetic than her reputation.

events.title: Last Evenings on Earth
events.headline: A Cruise Ship and an Artificial Storm
events.location: Aboard the Free Breeze, off Australia
events.summary: After the São Paulo events, Regulus and Vertin board a cruise ship off the Australian coast, the Free Breeze. Regulus and Ulrich are testing an 'artificial Storm' with a unique record, also called 'Regulus', while Vertin suspects the remnants of Manus Vindictae have taken the ship for some unknown purpose. Elsewhere, Ms. Grace tries to use the chaos to persuade the Nukutai people to join Manus Vindictae.
events.critique: A bridging story that carries the plot between chapters and plants the idea that the Storm might be manufactured.

events.title: Showdown in Chinatown
events.headline: A Rookie, a Sergeant and a Vigilante
events.summary: In 1990s Los Angeles, a special LAPD unit that handles Arcanist crime pairs Sergeant Poitier with a rookie Vigil from the Foundation, Liang Yue. Poitier is sceptical at first and warms as she helps defuse tense moments across Chinatown. Then comes their biggest case. Hong Kong director Noire is in town filming her next movie, a vigilante called the Nightpiercer is killing people judged to have escaped punishment, using techniques from Detective C07, the heroine of Noire's earlier trilogy, and a reel of test footage has vanished from the Foundation's vault of arcane objects, possibly linked to Noire. Can Liang Yue find the Nightpiercer before Noire is added to the list?
events.critique: Genre pastiche with a clever hook: a killer whose methods come from fiction, and a director whose fiction becomes evidence.

events.title: 1987: Cosmic Overture
events.headline: One Last Launch
events.summary: Plesetsk, 1987. With Laplace cutting funding for the Russian cosmodrome, Hissabeth and Pointer make one last desperate attempt to send an Arcanist into space to watch the Storm from a place it supposedly cannot touch but can be studied. Windsong directs the pair to an acrobat named Kiperina, who seems to meet every requirement for an astronaut recruit, Name Day arrives to help, and a mysterious mute girl who calls herself Voyager joins the troupe for reasons unknown.
events.critique: A story about the end of a funding line and the beginning of something stranger, with a silent newcomer as its open question.

events.title: The Midnight Whistle
events.headline: A Train Out of the War
events.location: The Danube Dawn, a train in wartime Europe
events.summary: Crowds try to board a train, the Danube Dawn, to escape the ravages of the Great War. It is run by a stern conductress named Corvus, who has no patience for bribes, begging or threats from those without tickets. One passenger, Semmelweis, has been sent by the Foundation to find out whether a vampire is on board and to stop it. Semmelweis takes pity on a red-eyed girl named Rubuska and lets her on in place of an absent investigator. Despite its reputation as a safe haven for paying refugees, the train soon holds mysteries Semmelweis did not expect, among them the wild card Rubuska, who says she is a vampire but is an Arcanist of a different kind.
events.critique: The closed train is a reliable stage, and here it carries a good reversal: the supposed monster turns out to be a different category of problem.

events.title: A Flowing Feast
events.headline: A Diamond, a Diviner and a City Losing Its Mind
events.summary: The Vigiles Bureau questions Adele Tavernier, an Arcanist and Paris taxi driver of the 1930s, about the events leading up to the Storm and the whereabouts of Beryl Bouanich, a diviner the Foundation considers a major person of interest. Adele uses her arcane skill and her tiny dragon, Feufeu, to expose fake diviners between fares. A regular customer, the wealthy Félicienne, asks her to visit Beryl, which Adele cannot do. Then she stumbles across Beryl's shop on her own and acquires the French Blue, a diamond thought lost since the French Revolution, while receiving visions of a university friend telling her not to give it to anyone. Meanwhile the city's streets are going mad: residents argue about the Bourbons and the Paris Commune, others report the Beasts of Gévaudan eating people in the street, and Félicienne keeps appearing and vanishing in Adele's visions. Professor Roseau insists it is all in her head, while Adele struggles to keep hold of herself, and to tell reality from delusion, as the Manus make their move in Paris.
events.critique: An interrogation frame gives the story an unreliable narrator, and Paris itself becomes the haunted object. The tension between a professor's rationalism and a city's collective hallucination is the story's real argument.

events.title: Spring Unending
events.headline: A Reporter in Search of Longer Life
events.summary: Reed, a UTTU reporter and a personified Yao, follows a rumour from an online chatroom to China, looking for Zhu County and the Method of Longevity. No one in the town seems to know of either. Partly for the story and partly to extend her own short lifespan, Reed walks every inch of the town until one night her memory is carried back to ancient times, where she witnesses the tale of the apparently immortal Paper Heron, a grass-like Yao named Mayfly, and the School of Mei, which sought the same Method of Longevity she is chasing.
events.critique: A story about mortality told through a short-lived protagonist, with the ancient flashback giving the present-day search a mirror.

events.title: The Turquoise Serpent Club
events.headline: A Grave Keeper, a Pigment and a Secret Party
events.summary: Foundation agent Loggerhead investigates Manus Vindictae activity in Mexico City. The Vigiles Bureau resents her presence but directs her to a grave keeper named Ramona, who reluctantly agrees to work with her. Meanwhile, the enigmatic Lorentz Butterfly is chasing an Arcane power source hidden in an unusual pigment. Both lines of inquiry lead to a secretive gathering, the Turquoise Serpent Club, hosted by a criminal known only as Senor Perez.
events.critique: A convergent plot: two investigations from different directions meeting at one invitation-only door.

events.title: Last and First Principles
events.headline: The Director Who Needs a Protocol
events.summary: Enigma, co-Acting Director of the LSCC, is exhausted on several fronts: the Foundation wants to install its own Director after Lucy's departure, the paperwork and requests never end, several researchers are demanding his attention, and the death of his sister Greta still weighs on him. On top of this, Madam Z asks him for a 'Pre-Storm Protocol' to prove he deserves the full-time Directorship before the Foundation's patience runs out and she can no longer placate the other board members. With few options left, and while pushing away suicidal thoughts, Enigma calls on fellow Laplace researchers Ulrich, Marcus and Medicine Pocket to re-enter Musae III's Toybox and unlock its source in order to finish a Pre-Storm Protocol report.
events.critique: An unglamorous premise, burnout in a bureaucracy, which gives Enigma more interiority than any battle would. The Toybox is a fitting setting for a man who has been working inside a puzzle for too long.

events.title: The Temporal Scale
events.headline: Ruins That Keep Their Memories
events.summary: Collapsed buildings in Eastern Europe still hold memories, and architects and supervisors walk through the ruins as the rubble refuses to stay silent. It is a quieter event than Chapter 13 and, in some ways, a heavier one: less about large battles than about what remains after the Storm has passed. Everecho's character story, 'A Fledgling's Brave Fall', is set inside this event.
events.critique: A deliberately small story after a large one. Where Chapter 13 asks what the cast will carry, this asks what the rubble remembers.

crossovers.title: La Primavera di Firenze
crossovers.headline: An Animus in All But Name
crossovers.summary: X tests his latest invention, remarkably like the Animus, and sends Vertin, APPLe and Sotheby to Renaissance Italy. Separated from the group, APPLe is about to be cut open by Leonardo da Vinci, who is acting under pressure from Knights Templar, when the assassin Ezio Auditore saves them both at the last moment. Vertin joins them, and Sotheby, who has been forcibly adopted by a Florentine noble, is part of the party. Together they try to solve a mystery about a series of fresco paintings, unaware that a local priest and patron, Father Alberto, who already works with the Templars, has set a trap. Vertin and Ezio must combine their skills to defeat him and close the case.
crossovers.critique: The conceit, a time-travel gadget standing in for a franchise's famous device, is the right way to graft two settings together, and the apple facing the surgeon is the story's best joke.

crossovers.title: Drama in Athens
crossovers.headline: A Drunk Apple at the Dionysia
crossovers.summary: Vertin and APPLe are projected into the past again, this time with Regulus rather than Sotheby. They land in Athens during the Peloponnesian War. APPLe, drunk on local wine, ends up in a basket destined as a sacrifice at the Dionysia, the festival of Dionysus. Vertin and Regulus, in an era where their knowledge of technology is useless, go looking for him and meet a mercenary named Kassandra, the Eagle Bearer, who is on a mission to protect Perikles from a cult that wants to kill him in the name of their Sage.
crossovers.critique: Comic premise, historical stakes, and a reliable engine: the heroes' modern knowledge turns out to be dead weight.

crossovers.title: Polymerized Dreams
crossovers.headline: A Convention Where the Machines Go Mad
crossovers.summary: Vertin, Mesmer Jr. and X use X's simulator to visit an alternate Soviet Union in which a plague swept the globe instead of the Second World War, and the Soviet Union rose as a great power thanks to a highly advanced polymer that accelerated everything from robotics to medicine. The trio enter as foreign scientists at a Soviet-hosted convention where Dr. Sechenov is about to unveil Kollektiv 2.0, a mass communication network that will link polymerized people, and soon the world, with their machines and each other almost instantly. While they explore the exhibition hall, the system goes haywire and turns several robots and attendees murderously insane. With help from the robot Twins, Left and Right, and a foul-mouthed Soviet agent codenamed P-3, Mesmer Jr. and X race for a cure for the madness spreading through the convention centre, while Vertin searches for the traitor who sabotaged Kollektiv and tries to make him undo it.
crossovers.critique: A cautionary tale about connectivity, which sits comfortably beside the main story's themes of control and consent, and the simulator frame keeps the tone detached enough for the genre jump.
